## Data and software

Climate grids will be obtained from the PRISM Climate Group and processed in R.
The analysis stack uses **terra**, **sf**, **ggplot2**, **dplyr**, and
**lubridate**. Geographic operations use explicit coordinate reference systems,
and every file path is relative to the project root.

Daily maximum temperature, minimum temperature, and precipitation are obtained
for Arizona and New Mexico with a 0.5-degree geographic buffer. Temperature is
retained in degrees Fahrenheit and precipitation in inches. The stable local
archive begins in 1981, while fixed 1991-2020 normals are used for standard
climate comparisons.

Daily temperature thresholds pool a centered five-day calendar window and use
R quantile type 8. February 29 thresholds are interpolated from February 28 and
March 1. A precipitation wet day is at least 0.04 inch; precipitation amount
percentiles are calculated from wet days rather than from all days including
zeros.

## Reproducible updates

Raw downloads, processed analysis files, and presentation-ready maps are kept in
separate directories. Quarto renders the static website to `_site/`. Shell
scripts in `scripts/` provide entry points for unattended Ubuntu execution and
S3 deployment; scheduling and AWS credentials remain external to this repository.

The repository's
[technical PRISM methods](../docs/prism-data-methods.md) document records the
periods, processing decisions, API safeguards, and function-level workflow.
